mainTopic: Identifying the offering in the ברייתא: why זבח is read as specific, why רב ששת rejects פסח and פסח שני, and the dispute over whether פסח שני overrides טומאה
overview: This amud joins the סוגיא in the middle of a discussion about a ברייתא. The ברייתא describes an offering that overrides שבת, overrides טומאה, and can have a תמורה. First the גמרא finishes explaining that 'זבח' in the ברייתא means one specific offering, not all sacrifices, because בכור and מעשר follow special rules. It then explains why תמורה can be one general category when זבח cannot. Next it asks why רב ששת does not explain the ברייתא as the קרבן פסח. The answer is that he holds אין שוחטין הפסח על היחיד. The פסח שני does not work either, because it does not override טומאה. Then רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רבא why the תנא calls the פסח a קרבן יחיד but the חגיגה a קרבן ציבור. רבא answers that it is because of פסח שני, and he accepts that this תנא follows רבי יהודה, who holds that פסח שני overrides טומאה. The amud ends with each side's reasoning: the תנא קמא's argument from logic and רבי יהודה's פסוק 'ככל חקת הפסח'.

steps.title: Firstborn and tithe show that 'offering' is not a general category
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. בכור and מעשר are exceptions, so the ברייתא is not teaching a general rule about all זבחים. It must be talking about one specific offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, a firstborn or an animal tithe: their holiness takes effect even on an animal with a permanent blemish, and they do not go out to non-sacred status to be sheared or worked. So the ברייתא is not teaching a general category of 'offering'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing an answer that started on the previous amud. It explains that the word 'offering' in the ברייתא cannot cover all sacrifices, because בכור and מעשר follow different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if someone consecrates an animal that already has a permanent blemish (מום קבוע), it gets only monetary holiness. Once redeemed, it becomes fully חולין and may be sheared and worked. בכור and מעשר are different: their holiness takes full hold even on a בעל מום קבוע, and they never go out to חולין for shearing or work. These are exactly the features the ברייתא credits to תמורה over זבח. So a broad contrast with 'all offerings' would be false, and the ברייתא must be pointing to one particular offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is automatically holy
An animal with a permanent blemish
To be sheared and to be used for work

steps.confusionAlert: בכור and מעשר are still holy offerings. The point is only that they have unusual rules about blemishes and redemption. So a general statement about 'every offering' would not fit them.

phrases.english: A firstborn and an animal tithe,
whose holiness takes effect even on a permanently blemished animal,
and they do not go out to non-sacred status
to be sheared and to be worked.
phrases.notes: An ordinary animal consecrated when already permanently blemished becomes fully חולין once redeemed, so it may be sheared and worked. בכור and מעשר never become permitted for this.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not teaching a general category of 'offering'.
phrases.notes: So 'offering' in the ברייתא refers to one specific offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began on the previous amud, about how to read the word 'offering' in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's wording as specific rather than general
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the ברייתא's 'offering' means a general category of all sacrifices.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because בכור and מעשר are exceptions, 'offering' must refer to one particular offering.

steps.title: Why treat substitution and offering differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא reads תמורה as a general category but זבח as one specific case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question that sets up the next answer. Why would the same ברייתא treat one word as a general category and the other word as a specific case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading has been inconsistent so far: 'תמורה' is taken broadly, while 'זבח' is taken narrowly. The גמרא wants a reason for treating the two words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution: trying to swap an ordinary animal for a holy one, which makes both holy

phrases.english: And what is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the inconsistency created by step 1's reading of זבח as a specific offering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why תמורה is read as a category while זבח is read as a specific offering.

steps.title: Substitution is uniform; offerings have exceptions
steps.stepSummary: תמורה works the same way in every case, so it can be one category. Offerings include בכור and מעשר, which follow different rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Substitution is one single category. But with offerings, there is the firstborn and there is the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A general category works for תמורה but not for זבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case of תמורה follows the same rules, so a general statement about it is accurate. Offerings are not uniform, because בכור and מעשר have their own special rules. That is why 'offering' has to mean one specific case.

phrases.english: Substitution is one single category of substitution.
Offering: there is the firstborn
and there is the tithe.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמורה is uniform, so it can be a category. Offerings include exceptions like בכור and מעשר, so 'זבח' must be specific.
steps.whatToRemember: A word can be read as a general rule only if every case under it follows the same law. תמורה passes that test. זבח does not, because of בכור and מעשר.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב ששת explain the ברייתא as the Paschal offering?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the ברייתא means אילו של אהרן. The גמרא asks why he doesn't say it means the קרבן פסח, which also overrides שבת and טומאה and can have a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב ששת: instead of explaining the ברייתא as the ram of אהרן, let him explain it as the Paschal offering. It overrides שבת and טומאה, and one can make a substitution with it, since it is an individual's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's reading. Another offering, the קרבן פסח, seems to fit the ברייתא's description just as well, or even better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a קרבן יחיד (an individual's offering) can have a תמורה. The ברייתא needs an offering that overrides שבת, overrides טומאה, and can have a תמורה. The קרבן פסח seems to meet all three conditions. So why did רב ששת choose the כהן גדול's ram?

keyTerms.meaning: The ram of אהרן: the כהן גדול's ram offering on יום כיפור

phrases.english: And according to Rav Sheshet,
rather than establishing it as the ram of Aaron,
let him establish it as the Paschal offering,
which overrides Shabbat and ritual impurity
and can make a substitution,
since it is an individual's offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת, אַדְּמוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּאֵילוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן, לוֹקְמַהּ בְּפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new question: which offering רב ששת should say the ברייתא is describing.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's explanation that the ברייתא refers to אילו של אהרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרבן פסח seems to fit all three features in the ברייתא, so there is no clear need to pick the כהן גדול's ram.

steps.title: רב ששת holds the Paschal offering is not slaughtered for one person
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds אין שוחטין הפסח על היחיד. So the קרבן פסח is not a true individual's offering and cannot have a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that one does not slaughter the Paschal offering for a single individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב ששת. The קרבן פסח does not fit the ברייתא, because in his view it is never brought by one person alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קרבן פסח must be brought by a group, it is at least a partnership offering, not a קרבן יחיד. Only an individual's offering can have a תמורה. So the קרבן פסח fails the 'makes a תמורה' condition, and רב ששת had to pick a different offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The Paschal offering is not slaughtered for a single individual

phrases.english: He holds:
one does not slaughter the Paschal offering for an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the underlying halachic position of the אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קרבן פסח is an individual's offering and fits the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב ששת, the קרבן פסח is always a group offering, so it cannot have a תמורה.
steps.confusionAlert: The קרבן פסח is still a private offering, not a community offering. The point is only that it needs more than one person, so it is not a 'single individual's' offering for the rules of תמורה.

steps.title: Then explain it as the פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסח שני, which may be brought by a single individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him establish it as the פסח שני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with another candidate. The פסח שני can be brought by one person, so maybe it fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the regular קרבן פסח was that it needs a group. The פסח שני is brought by an individual, so it seems to get around that problem. The challenge now is whether it meets the ברייתא's other conditions.

keyTerms.meaning: The second פסח, brought a month later by someone who missed the first
Let him establish it (as referring to)

phrases.english: And let him establish it as the second Pesach!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 5's answer but offers an alternative offering that avoids its problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's choice of אילו של אהרן, given step 5's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסח שני is brought by an individual, so the reason for rejecting the קרבן פסח does not apply to it.

steps.title: The second Pesach does not override impurity
steps.stepSummary: The פסח שני does not override טומאה, so it fails one of the ברייתא's conditions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a rhetorical question. The פסח שני cannot be what the ברייתא means, because it is not offered in a state of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires an offering that overrides טומאה. The פסח שני does not, so it fails that test. This leaves רב ששת's explanation, אילו של אהרן, standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it override? (a rhetorical question meaning 'it does not')

phrases.english: Does it override ritual impurity?
phrases.notes: He's asking to make a point: it doesn't.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the proposed case fails one of the required conditions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח שני, as an individual's offering, could fit the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח שני does not override טומאה, so רב ששת keeps אילו של אהרן.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's offering must meet three conditions: it overrides שבת, it overrides טומאה, and it can have a תמורה (so it must be a קרבן יחיד). The קרבן פסח fails the individual condition, and the פסח שני fails the טומאה condition. That is why רב ששת says it is אילו של אהרן.

steps.title: Why is the פסח called an individual offering but the חגיגה a communal one?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רבא why the תנא calls the פסח a קרבן יחיד and the חגיגה a קרבן ציבור, since both are brought by large crowds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רבא: According to the תנא, what makes the פסח different, that he calls it an individual's offering? And what makes the חגיגה different, that he calls it a communal offering? If it is because the חגיגה comes with a crowd, the פסח also comes with a crowd!
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב הונא points out what looks like an inconsistency in how the תנא labels the פסח and the חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The natural reason to call the חגיגה 'communal' is that the whole nation brings it together. But the whole nation also brings the פסח together. So why does the פסח get the 'individual' label?

keyTerms.meaning: The festival peace-offering brought on the holiday (here, the one eaten with the פסח)
A gathering or crowd; the whole people together

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rava:
And the tanna: what is different about the Pesach offering
that he calls it an individual's offering,
and what is different about the Chagigah
that he calls it a communal offering?
If it is because it comes with a crowd,
phrases.notes: That is, the חגיגה is brought by the whole nation together.

phrases.english: the Pesach also comes with a crowd!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא: וְתַנָּא, מַאי שְׁנָא פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of questioning about how the תנא classifies offerings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא's labeling of the פסח as a קרבן יחיד and the חגיגה as a קרבן ציבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'brought by a crowd' makes an offering communal, then the פסח should be communal too.

steps.title: Because פסח שני is not brought by a crowd
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that there is פסח שני, which is not brought by a crowd. That is why the פסח is not called communal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is פסח שני, which does not come with a crowd.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. Not every פסח is a crowd offering, because פסח שני is brought by scattered individuals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסח is brought by everyone, but פסח שני is brought only by the few people who missed the first one. Since the פסח as a category includes this non-crowd version, the תנא labels it an individual offering. The חגיגה has no such version.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'second פסח' on 14 אייר, for those who could not bring the first one

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי דְּלָא אָתֵי בְּכִנּוּפְיָא.
phrases.english: There is the second Pesach, which does not come with a crowd.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי דְּלָא אָתֵי בְּכִנּוּפְיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: one version of the category (פסח שני) lacks the crowd feature.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח is always a crowd offering, just like the חגיגה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because פסח שני is not a crowd offering, the תנא calls the פסח an individual's offering.

steps.title: Then פסח שני should override שבת and impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges back: if so, פסח שני should override שבת and טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, it should override שבת and טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא attacks רבא's answer. If the תנא's label depends on פסח שני, then פסח שני should share the פסח's power to override שבת and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא treats the פסח as an offering that overrides שבת and טומאה. If his reason for the 'individual' label rests on פסח שני, then פסח שני must be included in that same framework. That would mean it overrides טומאה too, which seems surprising.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,

phrases.aramaic: יְהֵא דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְאֶת הַטּוּמְאָה!
phrases.english: it should override Shabbat and ritual impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם כֵּן יְהֵא דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְאֶת הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing פסח שני into the תנא's framework would force the surprising conclusion that it overrides טומאה.

steps.title: Yes, this תנא holds פסח שני overrides impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the result: yes, this תנא follows the opinion that פסח שני does override טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, he follows the one who says it overrides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not back down. He agrees that this תנא really does hold that פסח שני overrides טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of escaping the challenge, רבא accepts its conclusion. He shows that this view is a known opinion among the תנאים, so it is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
it is according to the one who says it overrides,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר דָּחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by accepting its conclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge's conclusion and attributing the תנא to a known opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It would be absurd for פסח שני to override טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא holds the view that פסח שני does override טומאה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the dispute about פסח שני and impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: the תנא קמא says פסח שני overrides שבת but not טומאה. רבי יהודה says it overrides טומאה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: פסח שני overrides שבת but does not override טומאה. רבי יהודה says: it even overrides טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that there really is an opinion that פסח שני overrides טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that פסח שני overrides שבת. They argue only about טומאה. רבי יהודה is the 'one who says it overrides' that רבא was relying on.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The תנא who holds that פסח שני overrides טומאה

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: As it was taught: The second Pesach overrides Shabbat,
but it does not override ritual impurity.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It even overrides ritual impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's claim in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That an opinion exists holding פסח שני overrides טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: This seems to clash with step 7, which said פסח שני does not override טומאה. That answer followed the תנא קמא. Here רבא is placing our תנא with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The תנא קמא's reason: impurity is why he got a second chance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the תנא קמא's reason: the whole reason he is bringing פסח שני is that טומאה pushed off his first פסח, so how can he now bring it while impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא? He would tell you: טומאה pushed him off the first time, and now he should bring it in טומאה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא's view and gives it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני exists because a person was impure at the time of the first פסח. It would be self-defeating to let the second one be brought in that same impurity. So for the תנא קמא, פסח שני does not override טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?
He would say to you: because of impurity they pushed him off,
and now it should be done in impurity?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of one side of the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind the תנא קמא's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since impurity is the very reason for פסח שני, it cannot be brought in impurity.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's verse: like all the laws of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the פסוק 'ככל חקת הפסח יעשו אותו' that פסח שני follows all the rules of the first פסח, so it can even be brought in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה would tell you: the פסוק says, 'According to all the law of the פסח they shall do it,' and that includes even in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives רבי יהודה's source. It is a פסוק that compares פסח שני to the first פסח in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסח, which is brought by the community, can be brought in טומאה. 'ככל חקת הפסח' tells us פסח שני copies all its laws. So פסח שני also overrides טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to all the law of the פסח (במדבר ט:יב)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר לָךְ, אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say to you: the verse says:
"According to all the statute of the Pesach they shall do it,"
meaning even in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר לָךְ, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side's source, parallel to step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסח שני follows all the laws of the first פסח, including being brought in טומאה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה answers the תנא קמא's logic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers the תנא קמא's argument: the Torah gave the person another chance to bring it in purity, and if he did not get that chance, he brings it in impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah came back to him to let him do it in purity. If he did not merit that, he should do it in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה responds to the תנא קמא's point from step 13. The second chance is a bonus opportunity for purity, not a rule that forbids impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא thought it was self-defeating to bring פסח שני in טומאה. רבי יהודה says the Torah's goal was only to give the person another shot at bringing it pure. If that does not work out, the פסח is still brought, even in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Came back to him (gave him another chance)

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: פסח שני overrides שבת but not טומאה, since impurity is why it exists. רבי יהודה: it overrides טומאה too, because of 'ככל חקת הפסח'. The second chance is for purity if possible, and otherwise even in impurity. Our תנא, who calls the פסח a קרבן יחיד because of פסח שני, follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: The Torah came back to him
so he could do it in purity;
if he did not merit that, he should do it in impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהודה's position by answering the תנא קמא's reasoning in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the purpose of פסח שני.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since impurity caused the delay, פסח שני cannot be brought in impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח שני is a chance to bring it pure. If that fails, it is brought in impurity.
